notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.
Circuit as drawn: Vidor pin 2 -> green wire -> breadboard column 3 -> 82 ohm resistor (columns 3 to 6) -> LED anode (column 6). LED cathode (column 8) -> black wire -> Vidor GND.
The breadboard image has rows f-j on the half nearest the top. The catalogue names that half bank 'b', so the holes are written as 3b.g, 3b.h, 6b.h, 6b.i, 8b.i and 8b.h.

The LED's bent (longer) leg is taken as the anode and sits in column 6, next to the resistor. The straight leg is the cathode in column 8. The LED legs are placed in row i. The resistor and the black wire are in row h, and the green wire is in row g. Each pair shares a column strip.
The Vidor's pin 2 is written with the catalogue port name D2. The resistor limits the LED current and sits on the anode side, as in the image.
The USB cable is not shown in the manual's circuit, so it is not included.
